omission_summary.description: Imaging stage/association repair: o_image and flow:io:input:o_image:s_encoded allow inspection during either flow, but s_encoded is the output of completed A/B ligation and second-chip removal. First-flow imaging occurs before the first chip is removed. Narrow this represented occurrence and its condition to the supported completed-B/post-second-chip image, or represent earlier inspections with their actual input stages. Keep the general during-flow capability source-qualified; do not imply completed A/B material already exists during A flow. This corrects an asserted material-stage association used by the optional anatomy-registration route.

It currently gives SU-8 inventory/mold thickness and PDMS recipe, but omits the 50 μm chrome photomask/soft-lithography boundary, manufacturer-delegated photolithography/development/hard-bake steps and cut/peel/punch completion. Apart from Nextera XT FC-131-1024, most listed catalogue identities are missing (including dNTP R0192, inhibitors Y9240L/AM2694, ligase M0202L, AMPure A63880, KAPA KK2601, Proteinase K EO0491, and the primary buffer identities B7203S/B0202S). Known reagent roles and interfaces remain supported, so this detail repair is nonblocking for architecture but still requires record revision.

Revised severity labels differ, but this pair demonstrates no detection gain. Revised arm visibly used joined neighborhood inspection; baseline succeeded with separate views.

additional_findings_assessment.assessment: Both reviewers identify actual missing catalogue annotations that are available in primary p00134 and supplemental p00005/p00007. The frozen unconditional SO-REAGENT-INVENTORY requests them. This is a ledger-specific detail completeness observation, not an added chemical/routing error or an independently established requirement for the general assay architecture. Do not count it as a false positive or a new invention failure without defining evaluation scope.

Both reviewers identify absent photomask and cut/peel/punch details available in primary p00034/p00035 under the selected optional fabrication obligation. The candidate already describes manufacturer-delegated SU-8 processing, so the revised request to enumerate named delegated substeps may ask for finer wording within that existing boundary. These are nonblocking equipment-detail suggestions, not evidence that finished-chip interfaces are missing.

Both primary reviews mark the two detail additions blocking=false but action=revise_record. Current review_outcome treats any revise_record action as needs_revision. The timing defect independently warrants revision here, so this pair cannot establish the detail-only gate effect or optimal scope policy.

limitations: One unreplicated sequential pair on an exposed development case; no reliability estimate, significance test or causal prompt-performance claim.
Control labels were model-authored then source-checked; they are not independent wet-lab expert gold.
Mechanical target/field/quote completeness is distinct from semantic truth of every positive claim. Only the named controls and additional findings were source-assessed in this audit.
The source-requirement ledger can itself overstate necessary granularity; both arms were held to the same frozen ledger, not tuned to their outputs.
Reported token usage is native aggregate accounting across context turns, including repeated/cached input; this audit establishes neither unique-paper tokens nor billed account/cost.

No named query call was observed; equivalent programmatic neighborhood inspection is directly visible in the revised arm. Presence of a prompt alone is not evidence of compliance or private reasoning.

Audit maps recorded remote execution prefixes to local copied outputs and rechecks their pinned bytes. It does not independently inspect live Sherlock or claim original-document closure beyond these copied evidence inputs.
The two negative targets are correlated representations of one timing-association defect, not two independent error discoveries.
